#5179. Ripple's XRP Ledger Lending to Receive Repayment Fix

The XRP Ledger's lending protocol is in for a tidy-up of how loan repayments get rounded. In plain terms, the balance after each payment would match the schedule, the update has been discribed in the official Github pull request.

After an overpayment, TotalValueOutstanding is reset to the scheduled value of the new PeriodicPayment.

Under the LendingProtocolV1_2 amendment, each on-time LoanPay would bring TotalValueOutstanding down to the scheduled value with one payment fewer, capped at the rounded PeriodicPayment.

The first commit moves the scheduled-value calculation out of computeLoanProperties into a separate scheduledValue function, with no behavior change.

That way, LoanSet and LoanPay round it the same way. Zero-interest loans also need a floor on the principal part, because their value is rounded to nearest while the principal is rounded up. Tests run on Legacy, CashBasis and FixedPrecision vaults, with and without the amendment.

Today, each payment's value part is calculated on its own, so rounding can build up across payments. The last payment can then need one unit more than the rounded PeriodicPayment, and the value parts can alternate between payments.

With the change, a method called telescoping makes the value part of every on-time payment either the floor or the ceiling of PeriodicPayment, and at least one unit. The last payment becomes exactly the rounded PeriodicPayment.

There's little to no effect for users and investors today. The extra unit on the final payment changes little. Older loans that already carried one unit above their schedule simply keep it, so the last payment still needs the PeriodicPayment and a single unit, unless the borrower overpays first.

Small overpayments are mostly ignored; the transaction goes through successfully and charges no extra XRP whatsoever.

Activation date is yet to be determined: 80% of validators agreement is needed for two weeks in a row for the amendment to go through. No public vote for LendingProtocolV1_2 has been announced yet, so the timeline remains uncertain.

#5177. Coinbase Explains Cold-Storage Defences After Binance Breach Shakes Crypto Industry

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Coinbase says it was not affected by the reported Binance hot-wallet incident and that more than 99% of customer assets are kept in cold storage. The exchange outlined controls around signing, withdrawal limits and suspicious activity, offering a useful test of how custodians should explain security practices.

A major attack on one exchange inevitably prompts customers elsewhere to ask the same question: where are my assets actually held, and what stops them being moved without permission? Coinbase addressed those concerns in a November 4 security explanation, published against the backdrop of the reported Binance incident.

In its official post, Coinbase said it had not been affected by the breach and that more than 99% of customer assets were held in cold storage. It also described distributed signing keys, withdrawal limits, anomaly detection and emergency controls capable of stopping transaction signing.

Cold storage refers broadly to arrangements designed to keep signing authority away from routine internet-connected systems. It can reduce the exposure of a custodian’s largest reserves if a hot wallet or application layer is compromised. Hot wallets remain useful for normal withdrawals, so the balance between operational liquidity and offline custody matters.

The reported percentage is Coinbase’s stated current practice; it should not be interpreted as a universal guarantee that every customer balance is insulated from every type of problem. Account takeover, internal controls, fraud, software defects and legal restrictions are separate categories of risk. A security system is strongest when the organisation explains the entire chain of access rather than relying on one impressive percentage.

Similarly, distributed keys can mean that no single compromised system can authorise a large movement, but only if the policy around those keys is well implemented. Limits and anomaly detection add further layers, potentially buying time when a transaction looks unusual.

Custodians face an awkward operational challenge. Users expect transfers to work continuously, but allowing automated movement from the internet-connected part of a system increases the consequences of a compromise. A good model therefore combines preventative controls with monitoring and rehearsed incident procedures.

The disclosure comes as industry participants investigate the reported multi-billion-dollar Binance exploit and as stablecoin issuers describe the actions available to them once assets have left a platform. These are connected but distinct defences: custody aims to stop unauthorised signing, while downstream tracing and freezes aim to limit damage after funds move.

The importance of resilience is also visible in decentralised finance. As NewsBTC reported when Aave restricted new tBTC supply and borrowing, operational controls can reduce further exposure during an incident. They are most useful when their scope is explicit and their effect is independently checked.

Useful questions include whether balances are fully backed, what proportion is held in internet-connected wallets, how withdrawals are approved, whether controls are independently assessed, and how the company communicates if access is interrupted. A customer should also understand the difference between assets held by a platform and tokens in a wallet whose private keys they personally control.

Coinbase’s statement offers concrete details rather than simply calling itself secure. Those details still need to be assessed over time against audits, incident disclosures and actual operational performance. The wider lesson is that custody design belongs at the centre of an exchange’s risk story, not in small print below a trading app.

An anonymous Tornado Cash whale sent $7 million to Hyperliquid to open a large long on Bitcoin this morning. According to Lookonchain and Onchain Lens, the wallet went in with aggressive 20x leverage with the plan to profit from Bitcoin crushing Ether.

Large holders usually run funds through mixers to move capital privately or to get ready to cash out. This case is unusual as the movement of these funds had just previously been tracked to a chain of addresses belonging to the hackers who drained the derivatives platform Drift Protocol of $290 million in April 2026.

Some blockchain researchers warn against jumping to conclusions about where the funds came from. There's still no direct evidence: Tornado Cash covers its tracks well, and the link between the wallet and specific hacks rests only on circumstantial matches in volume.

After starting as a brand-new address that withdrew 3,100 ETH from Tornado Cash, the unknown later swapped all of the Ether through CoW Swap on the spot, locking in $6.92 million in USDC. From there, the money went to the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid as collateral for future trades.

On the exchange, the whale didn't try to guess where the market was headed and just split the collateral in half, turned on 20x cross leverage and built a position worth about $26 million in total. The position consisted of $12.84 million at an entry price of $75,762.2 and an Ethereum short of 5,740 ETH worth $12.83 million.

So far, the bet is working. Bitcoin is holding near local highs, and the gain on the BTC long fully covers the drawdown from altcoin short. Add to this the earnings on funding, collecting a regular premium from other traders for holding the ETH short.

This is a textbook dominance pair trade, where the investor couldn't care less whether the industry as a whole goes up or down and the only thing that matters is the spread - the price gap between the two largest coins.

If Bitcoin rises faster than Ether, or if Ether falls harder than Bitcoin in a broad market crash, the trade profits.

The math is elegant, but 20x leverage is always a high risk. Should Ethereum rip higher while Bitcoin stays stuck in a range, the margin will be wiped out in seconds as Hyperliquid's cross-margin system will force-close the orders, and the investor will lose the entire $6.92 million. The liquidation price is set at $37,014.09 for BTC and $3,343.60 for ETH.

#5173. Riot Sells More Than 20,000 Bitcoin as AI Data-Centre Contracts Reach $38B

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Riot Platforms says it sold 20,264 BTC in the first nine months of 2026, raising about $1.5 billion primarily for data-centre development. Its latest quarterly release puts long-term contracted data-centre revenue at around $38 billion, underlining how far the miner’s business model is shifting.

Riot Platforms has made a striking choice with its Bitcoin holdings: sell a substantial amount of the asset it mines to finance the infrastructure it hopes will deliver future revenue. That strategy is clearer than ever in its third-quarter results, released November 4.

In its earnings filing, Riot said it sold 20,264 Bitcoin year to date for approximately $1.5 billion, mainly to fund data-centre construction. The company also announced a 15-year powered-land lease for 910 critical IT megawatts at its Corsicana campus, representing about $28 billion of contractual value over the initial term.

Riot recorded $181.4 million in third-quarter revenue, barely above the comparable quarter a year earlier. Bitcoin mining contributed $116 million, down from $160.8 million, even though production increased to 1,637 BTC from 1,406 BTC. The company attributes much of the decline in mining revenue to a lower average realised Bitcoin price during the quarter.

At the same time, engineering revenue rose to $47 million and data-centre revenue was $18.4 million. Those lines make the transition visible in the income statement, although the extraordinary long-term lease figures are not the same as cash already earned. They depend on delivery milestones, counterparties, the terms of each agreement and years of operations.

Riot says it has now leased 1,151 MW of critical IT capacity, with roughly $38 billion of long-term contracted revenue. Investors should distinguish that total contract value from current profit, and consider what future capital expenditure may be required to bring the facilities online.

The Bitcoin sales create resources that can fund land, power connections, construction and specialised infrastructure. They also reduce direct exposure to future Bitcoin appreciation. It is a deliberate decision to exchange part of a liquid treasury asset for a business with potentially steadier contracted revenues, but one that carries construction and customer concentration risks.

Riot said it ended September with $950.2 million of cash and Bitcoin, including 2,418 BTC. It reported no equity raised during 2026, a detail relevant to shareholders concerned about dilution as build-outs expand.

Mining economics are still important. Riot reported an average cost to mine Bitcoin of $39,265 excluding depreciation, influenced by power-curtailment credits. Such credits are valuable, but energy arrangements and pricing can change. Our earlier look at Bitcoin miners’ growing AI commitments explored the same industry-wide tension between holding coins and building something new.

The milestones that matter most are construction progress, delivery of contracted megawatts, tenant payments and conversion of headline lease values into recurring revenue. A business can accumulate an impressive contract pipeline while facing sizeable financing, permitting or execution obstacles.

Riot’s disclosure shows that Bitcoin mining companies are not necessarily behaving like Bitcoin holding companies. One of the industry’s biggest operators is increasingly using the mined asset as a funding source for a different kind of data-centre business. That may eventually diversify earnings, but the timing and profitability have to be proven in cash flow rather than headlines.

Stalling XRP ETF net inflows have worsened the situation too. This month, for example, the ETFs had only one day of outflows, with the rest of the days being inactive. All these factors precipitated XRP’s sharp descent to $1.15.

Still, all may not be lost, with XRP’s price still holding above $1.15. The buying volume exceeded that of sellers too, hinting at a breakdown in selling pressure.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse’s ‘North Star’ comments during the Ripple Swell event about XRP and the XRP Ledger have kept some optimism going around too.

CEO Brad Garlinghouse has repeatedly described XRP and the XRP Ledger as Ripple’s ‘North Star,’ which serves as the core purpose and guiding principle of the company.

This was his response in the context of whether the Ripple USD [RLUSD] stablecoin is shifting focus away from the chain’s native token, XRP. According to the exec, RLUSD is merely competing with other stablecoins.

Additionally, the $1.15-level was the last lower high before a market structure shift turned XRP bullish. Hence, the ongoing decline could just be a retest of the structure shift. Only time will tell if that’s true though.

In case XRP falls below the level, the next demand zone would be $0.98.

#5171. DarkSword iPhone Exploit Drains $4M in Crypto Theft

Home » Crypto Market News » DarkSword iPhone Exploit Drains $4M in Crypto Theft

Zero-click browser vulnerability drains millions from unpatched devices by targeting stored recovery phrases.

A silent zero-click exploit chain targeting iPhones has drained more than $4 million in cryptocurrency across 365 TRON wallets, according to a report by Bitquery.

Dubbed DarkSword, the sophisticated attack kit compromises unpatched iOS devices through Safari—allowing hackers to extract private keys and seed phrases without requiring a single transaction signature or app download.

DarkSword, a kit for hacking iPhones, chains six iOS vulnerabilities to hijack devices running iOS 18.4 through 18.7. It compromises vulnerable iPhones through malicious websites opened in Apple’s Safari browser.

The exploit chain combines multiple security vulnerabilities to gain access to sensitive device information without requiring users to download an application or authorize a wallet transaction.

Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), together with cybersecurity firms Lookout and iVerify, published technical analyses of the exploit on March 18, 2026. Their findings describe an attack chain capable of accessing passwords, messages, and cryptocurrency wallet information stored in Apple’s Keychain.

A separate investigation by cybersecurity firm Censys identified modules targeting 18 cryptocurrency wallet applications. The toolkit can reportedly search photos and note-taking applications for recovery phrases, potentially exposing wallets whose credentials were stored on the device.

Targeted applications reportedly include MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, and Coinbase. The vulnerability lies in the iPhone’s operating system rather than the individual wallet applications.

Unlike conventional phishing attacks, DarkSword does not necessarily require victims to connect their wallets or approve suspicious transactions. Attackers who obtain a private key or recovery phrase can use another device to sign and broadcast transactions.

Bitquery’s investigation identified a network of 43 collection addresses connected through a shared fee wallet. The addresses received funds from 365 TRON wallets between October 5 and November 4.

The investigation found that at least $4.06 million in USDT was transferred. Of the 365 wallets affected, the median loss was $1,029. Eight wallets lost more than $100,000 each, accounting for 63% of the total USDT losses. The attackers reportedly sent small amounts of TRX to victims’ wallets shortly before draining their balances.

Bitquery traced the transfers back to an initial transaction whose amount and timing matched those of a publicly reported iPhone theft. However, blockchain records cannot reveal which devices or wallet applications individual victims were using.

Apple has released security updates addressing the vulnerabilities used by DarkSword. Google recommends installing the latest available iOS version or enabling Apple’s Lockdown Mode when an update is not possible.

Changing wallet passwords or revoking token approvals is not sufficient if attackers already possess the recovery phrase. A compromised seed requires generating a new one and transferring the assets.

DarkSword device-level attacks bypass wallet approval checks, so exposed seed phrases can lead to total loss without a single signature from the victim.

#5167. Hut 8 Expands AI Campus Commitments While Funding Buybacks With Bitcoin Sales

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Hut 8 says it fully commercialised its Beacon Point AI campus with a second 352 MW lease, taking expected aggregate base-term contract value across its AI data-centre portfolio to about $26.6 billion. The company also sold Bitcoin to fund share repurchases, showing how mining-era assets are being redeployed.

Hut 8’s third-quarter update is less about how many coins it mined and more about how much power, construction capacity and long-term tenant demand it can assemble. That represents a significant shift for a company long associated with Bitcoin infrastructure.

In its November 4 results, Hut 8 said a second 352-megawatt IT lease at Beacon Point fully commercialised the campus. It placed expected aggregate base-term contract value across its AI data-centre portfolio at about $26.6 billion and reported 1,330 MW of utility capacity under construction across its major AI projects.

The numbers describe commitments over years, not cash that has already appeared in the bank. Hut 8’s timetable includes an initial River Bend data-hall delivery target in the second quarter of 2027, followed by Beacon Point Phase 1 in the third quarter of 2027 and Phase 2 in the second quarter of 2028.

Those future dates matter. A contracted tenant can improve the business case for a development, but execution still depends on power availability, construction, testing, financing and customer readiness. The risk profile is not identical to Bitcoin mining, where machines may be deployed in stages and production responds directly to network conditions.

Hut 8 also reported 1,300 MW of additional energy capacity entering exclusivity, bringing that category to 3,180 MW. Exclusivity is a development milestone; it should not be interpreted as an operating facility or a guaranteed utility connection. Investors need to track the movement from a pipeline into actual delivered infrastructure.

The company said it bought back $74.7 million of shares during the quarter, funded with proceeds from selling approximately 954 Bitcoin. It later repurchased another $175.3 million of shares, funded through the sale of roughly 2,148 additional Bitcoin. Subsequent to the quarter, the repurchase authorisation increased to $1 billion.

That is a revealing capital-allocation decision. Selling Bitcoin to repurchase shares reduces treasury exposure to the coin while potentially increasing each remaining shareholder’s proportional interest in the company. Whether that creates value depends on the repurchase price and long-term performance of the business.

Hut 8 also closed a $1.07 billion senior secured revolving credit facility. The existence of a facility adds flexibility, but readers should distinguish committed borrowing capacity from cash revenue or money actually drawn. NewsBTC has previously examined the financing pressure created by miners’ AI expansion, and Hut 8 offers a clear example of how those choices reach the balance sheet.

Hut 8 has a substantial development pipeline and named delivery targets. The crucial tests will be whether those targets are met, whether project-level financing stays on acceptable terms and how much profit flows through when sites become operational.

The update captures a broader change in listed Bitcoin infrastructure businesses. Their market stories increasingly revolve around electricity access and long-term AI customers rather than the number of Bitcoin retained. That can produce a different revenue profile, but it does not remove the need for disciplined spending or independently verifiable execution.

#5165. Core Scientific’s AI Colocation Revenue Jumps to $215M as Mining Role Shrinks

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Core Scientific reported $215.4 million in third-quarter colocation revenue, nearly 60% above the prior quarter, while billing 485 MW of capacity. Its results show how an operator once known for Bitcoin mining is building a much larger business around contracted AI infrastructure.

Some Bitcoin mining companies have talked about their artificial-intelligence ambitions for years. Core Scientific’s latest financials show what that transition looks like once facilities begin producing substantial revenue from customers.

According to its November 5 earnings release, the company generated $215.4 million of colocation revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up from $136.7 million in the second quarter and $15 million a year earlier. Total quarterly revenue reached $232.9 million.

Core Scientific said it was billing for 485 megawatts as of September 30, representing more than $700 million in average annualised colocation GAAP revenue. That is a different unit of operating performance from hashrate or Bitcoin produced. It describes contracted power and computing infrastructure delivered to tenants.

The move is important because mining revenue depends on several volatile factors at once: Bitcoin price, network difficulty, block rewards and electricity costs. Colocation can offer a different mix of long-term contracts, infrastructure obligations and construction spending. The income stream may be easier to forecast after a facility is delivered, but the capital commitment can be enormous.

Core Scientific says it is approaching full delivery under its first colocation agreement and is constructing capacity under a second agreement across five campuses. Those claims are meaningful milestones, yet remaining construction work and billing ramps still matter to the final financial outcome.

The company reported approximately $1.18 billion in quarterly net income, but said the result benefited from a non-cash change in the fair value of warrants. That makes the headline profit figure a poor stand-in for recurring cash generated by running data centres.

Adjusted EBITDA was $133.6 million, more than three times the previous quarter’s $41.1 million, while capital expenditure reached $985.1 million. Both figures deserve attention. A rapidly growing operating business can still consume substantial cash as it adds the facilities needed to earn future contracted revenue.

This is a useful counterpoint to the more familiar NewsBTC discussion of Bitcoin miners’ AI pivot. The opportunity is becoming measurable, but comparing revenue without spending, financing and delivery schedules would make the transformation look easier than it is.

Investors should follow the number of megawatts actually billing, customer diversification, operating margins, remaining capital needs and any modifications to lease terms. A nominal pipeline is less revealing than a site whose systems have been accepted by a paying tenant.

The results also offer a warning against treating every company in this sector as an identical bet on Bitcoin’s price. Core Scientific now has a material infrastructure business whose fortunes may depend more on demand for AI compute and construction execution than on daily mining profitability. Its history remains part of the story, but the metrics are changing underneath it.

The predecessor of this story is the biggest cyberattack in history when, according to the FBI and Chainalysis, the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor emptied Binance's hot wallets for about $6.3 billion in a matter of 20 minutes. What happened next is the exchange blocking $3 billion with the help of Tether, Circle; its pledge to cover 100% of users' money from the SAFU fund; and thorough audits across Solana and Ethereum chains. Then, starting November 1, Binance started reopening tokens for withdrawal.

HYPE was the last to become eligible and the community behind DeFi giant met such a measure with discontent, crying about sabotage and unfair competition tactics. It's not that deep: Hyperliquid, being the headliner of decentralized finance, amasses a big share of the pie in on-chain derivatives trading, and of course this affects Binance's business.

The retaliation between the two has continued since 2025 when Hyperliquid founder Jeff Yan publicly accused Binance of lowering liquidations data after the October 10, 2025 event, when positions worth around $40 billion were marginally closed across the crypto market. Binance then delayed the spot listing of HYPE token until September 24, 2026 and gave it 'Seed Tag', which is usually applied to high-risk cryptocurrencies. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao diplomatically refused the accusations and said that strong decentralized exchanges on the contrary increase 'the pie' for the whole industry.

The delay indeed has a technical aspect. HYPE operates within its own Layer-1, HyperEVM. Auditing a custom blockchain architecture — not standard EVM or Solana-based — in the aftermath of such a hack requires more time and attention to be carried out properly.

In the wake of the cybersecurity crisis the pause was still interpreted as corporate vengeance. This makes Yi He's words and the demonstrative relaunch of withdrawals a sign that obligations for clients take priority over market rivalry.

A discussion regarding the throughput of major blockchains emerged after an X user, 'Minus Wells,' claimed that 1,500 TPS is not the future of finance, not even 5,000, adding that this is roughly Visa's average throughput on a normal day.

"1,500 TPS is not the future of finance, not even 5,000. Sorry, they lied to you for engagement. That's roughly Visa's average throughput on a normal day. Congrats on matching the legacy system," Wells wrote.

It's a process. 1) Not every transaction needs to be settled in seconds immediately. Payment channels or higher layers like Dassie (Interledger) are much better suited for mass (micro) payments. MasterCard is looking to do more hackathons afaik with the XRP Ledger after the successful one at Swell leveraging this and AI. Until: 2) I strongly believe we'll scale the L1s very sharply, not only XRPL, thanks to AI helping us to advance this tech even further. While Visa's network (VisaNet) has a technical capacity of 65,000 to over 83,000 transactions per second (TPS), its actual average volume runs at approximately 8,100 to 8,500 TPS. The post attracted attention in the XRP community given that the XRP Ledger sustains a throughput of 1,500 transactions per second (1,500 TPS) on commodity hardware.

Wells clarified he was not personally attacking XRP, claiming that XRPL, Avalanche, Stellar, Tezos L1, Cardano's Leios experiments, and OP Mainnet swap tests have all published throughput figures or results below 5,000 TPS. "Those aren't equivalent tests or necessarily current hard ceilings. But the question applies to everyone: can the infrastructure handle the demand future finance could bring?" he asked.

Hussein Zangana (Vet), XRP Ledger Foundation director of community, responded to claims regarding L1 blockchains' scalability with respect to XRP, saying "it's a process."

Vet made a case for the comparatively lower TPS of decentralized blockchains, noting that not every transaction needs to be settled in seconds. He pointed out that payment channels or higher layers like Dassie (Interledger) are much better suited for mass (micro) payments.

With respect to XRP, Vet noted that Mastercard is looking to do more hackathons with the XRP Ledger after a successful one at the Swell event while leveraging AI.

Batch, which allows multiple transactions to be bundled into a batch that is processed all together and was launched on the XRPL mainnet in October 2026, stands to benefit the XRP Ledger in this regard. "Batched settlement of institutions is good enough in the meantime to be very beneficial vs. TradFi," Vet added.

The XRP Ledger Foundation director of community highlighted massive scaling potential for the XRP Ledger and L1 blockchains.

"I strongly believe we'll scale the L1s very sharply, not only XRPL, thanks to AI helping us to advance this tech even further. We are continuously pushing throughput higher and there is a lot of potential (!!!) for significantly more," Vet wrote.

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Cipher Digital says it recognised its first high-performance-computing lease revenue in the third quarter of 2026 and extended its Barber Lake lease to 20 years, increasing contracted revenue to $9.1 billion. The milestone is about converting data-centre development into an operating business, not an instant cash windfall.

A signed data-centre lease and a functioning, revenue-producing facility are not the same achievement. Cipher Digital’s third-quarter update, released November 2, places the company at an important point between those stages.

In its official business update, the company said it recorded its first high-performance-computing, or HPC, lease revenue following the start of rent at Black Pearl. It also said the lease at Barber Lake had been extended to 20 years, raising its contracted revenue value to $9.1 billion.

The recognition of lease revenue shows that at least part of a project has advanced past development and into a billing relationship. It does not mean every planned data hall is operational. Cipher said multiple halls at Black Pearl and Barber Lake are scheduled to come online through year-end, so subsequent delivery remains central to the investment case.

High-performance computing infrastructure has different commercial characteristics from Bitcoin mining. Instead of purchasing machines primarily to win block rewards, the company develops sites intended to support customers’ demanding workloads under longer-term agreements. That can reduce some direct cryptocurrency market exposure while increasing dependency on construction schedules and individual tenants.

The length and total value of Barber Lake’s contract can help financiers evaluate future cash receipts. Still, contract value is not the same as revenue recognised in a quarter, cash available to shareholders or guaranteed profit. Operating expense, financing structure, maintenance and tenant performance all sit between those figures.

Cipher also reported conditional base-load classification for its 1-gigawatt Colchis project and early development of lateral pipelines intended to facilitate up to 2.5 GW of on-site generation for future expansion. These are large infrastructure ambitions, not facilities that have already delivered all their proposed capacity.

The central issue is access to reliable, affordable energy. Data-centre demand may be high, but sites cannot fulfil contracts without the supporting power network, cooling, equipment and permits. Companies that secured sites when they were focused on Bitcoin mining are trying to turn those physical advantages into AI capacity.

That shift has been a recurring theme in NewsBTC’s reporting on miners moving toward AI. Cipher’s results add a specific piece of evidence: its transition is no longer only a plan on a presentation slide, because some lease revenue has begun.

The next useful disclosures will show how much capacity has been accepted by customers, the revenue generated by each campus and the cost of completing construction. Readers should also check whether major contracts are concentrated among a small set of customers.

Cipher’s update is another reminder that Bitcoin-era data centres can develop into a very different asset class. Investors still need to judge whether the new use of that infrastructure will generate attractive returns after the enormous cost of building it. First lease revenue is a step forward, not the end of that assessment.

#5156. Circle’s USDC Transaction Volume Rises 49% Even as Reserve Income Faces Pressure

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Circle reported $13.9 trillion of USDC onchain transaction volume in the third quarter of 2026, up 49% year over year, while average USDC circulation reached $73.3 billion. The issuer’s results show strong network activity, but that does not translate directly into equivalent revenue growth.

Stablecoin businesses are often judged by a single number: how many dollars’ worth of tokens are circulating. Circle’s latest earnings suggest that approach misses a substantial part of what is happening around USDC, and also oversimplifies how the company makes money.

In its November 4 SEC-filed results, Circle reported $13.9 trillion in USDC onchain transaction volume for the quarter, an increase of 49% from a year earlier. Average USDC in circulation rose 8% to $73.3 billion, while total revenue and reserve income increased 17% to $865 million.

A stablecoin can move between users many times without the amount outstanding increasing. That makes onchain transfer volume a useful measure of network activity but a poor substitute for payment revenue, spending by real-world customers or income retained by the issuer.

Some onchain activity also reflects exchange settlement, liquidity management and transfers between controlled addresses. It would be a mistake to present $13.9 trillion as a tally of retail purchases or to assume the growth rate proves stablecoins have replaced ordinary banking payments.

Circle’s net income from continuing operations reached $226 million, up 5% year on year. Adjusted EBITDA increased 85% to $317 million. Differences in the growth rates reflect a changing mix of operational, distribution and accounting factors; investors should assess the underlying disclosures rather than treating all three numbers as interchangeable signals.

Circle highlighted that its payments network reached $41.3 billion in annualised total payment volume during the quarter. It also announced plans to acquire Tazapay, a cross-border payments platform, with completion expected in 2027 subject to approvals. These initiatives aim to make it easier for businesses to move between traditional payment systems and digital-dollar settlement.

This strategy faces a practical challenge: issuing a token is relatively simple compared with connecting a broad set of banking, compliance and payout arrangements. Customers require dependable redemption, useful local currency access and clear rules. Onchain transaction volumes alone do not tell us whether those services are profitable.

The competitive environment is also changing. As NewsBTC noted when some stablecoins faced new European trading restrictions, distribution is shaped by regulation as well as technology. An issuer needs both.

Beyond the headline USDC supply, the key numbers are revenue after distribution costs, payment volumes generated by identifiable services, changes in the reserve-income environment and the cost of expanding infrastructure. Circle has shown activity and profit growth, but it must continue converting that network usage into durable economics.

The bigger story is a maturing business model. Stablecoins increasingly compete as financial infrastructure, not simply as exchange trading pairs. Circle’s quarter offers evidence that USDC is moving at scale, while also reminding readers that volume, adoption and shareholder returns are three different questions.

Hyperliquid emerged as the most-viewed token in the last 24 hours, followed by Kinetiq [KNTQ], Bitcoin [BTC], and Pudgy Penguins [PENGU], respectively. At press time, the altcoin was trading at $77, with its daily trading volume hitting $442 million. What spurred this interest though?

Well, this spike in searches was fueled by some news from Binance. It announced the resumption of Hyperliquid [HYPE] and Aptos withdrawals following its late-October hack. It took the exchange 10 days to restart withdrawals.

Back when it was announced, the halt in services frustrated users despite Hyperliquid chain not being directly involved. Binance rectified the issue, citing that withdrawals had been paused to prevent assets from getting stuck in processing and/or loss of funds.

With services gradually resuming across the board, Binance has assured users they will continue to restore additional assets and networks in phases.

In fact, a couple of tokens have already been re-enabled, including altcoins and stablecoins on Ethereum [ETH] and Solana [SOL] networks. As far as HYPE is concerned, the timing here is interesting since the altcoin has been bearish since the crypto-exchange was hacked.

Institutions have been building their short positions, with that of Abraxas four times bigger than that of Wintermute. In fact, Abraxas’s perp exposure was in excess of $451 million, while Wintermute’s was about $107 million.

HYPE‘s $77.60 million short position was the second-largest for Abraxas, about half of Bitcoin’s at $158 million. The firm’s short positions were at an unrealized profit of more than $30.77 million.

Not only are some institutions selling, but so are smart traders. For instance, a whale sold 433K HYPE with a 10x leverage but seemed to be sitting on lifetime losses of about $20.92 million.

All these factors, together, have been piling on selling pressure on the token. In fact, this week’s candle eclipsed last week’s green candle that rallied from $76 and closed at $88.

At the time of writing, the altcoin was trading at around $75. This is a key support level that has been critical for hype since late August.

HYPE has fallen by over 12% in the last seven days, with the altcoin being among the worst altcoin performers in the market. The resumption of withdrawals on Binance could revive traders’ confidence and change broader crypto sentiment for the better.

However, if bears break below $75, HYPE could fall to $70 or $60, respectively.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Dogecoin cofounder Billy Markus shared a lighthearted observation about Japan's unique dog culture in a post on X, pointing out the popularity of Shiba Inu dogs in Japan.

"Like, 50% of the dogs I see in Japan are Shiba Inu," wrote Markus, who goes by the online handle Shibetoshi Nakamoto.

like 50% of the dogs i see in japan are shiba inu i love japan

The Dogecoin cofounder's comment is based on his own observation when he was in Japan, where the Shiba Inu breed has deep cultural roots and is still one of the country's most recognizable native dog breeds. Markus' observation is noteworthy, as he is the cofounder of Dogecoin, a cryptocurrency that draws its origins from the Shiba Inu dog.

On December 6, 2013, Dogecoin was launched, taking influence from the famous Doge meme: an image of a very adorable Shiba Inu dog with multi-colored Comic Sans text that appears as the dog's "thought bubbles."

This famous meme was based on a 2010 photograph of a Japanese female Shiba Inu dog, Kabosu, adopted by Japanese kindergarten teacher Atsuko Satō from an animal shelter in 2008. This helped establish the dog-themed cryptocurrency trend that later inspired several other tokens, including Shiba Inu (SHIB).

Kabosu, a Japanese Shiba Inu, inspired a generation of online jokes and became the face of Dogecoin cryptocurrency. Kabosu was the face of the breezy Doge meme, her quizzical expression surrounded by an inner monologue of choppy phrases in bad grammar written in rainbow-colored Comic Sans font.

In 2010, two years after adopting Kabosu from a puppy mill where she would otherwise have been put down, Ms. Satō, a teacher from Sakura, east of Tokyo, took a picture of her pet crossing her paws on the sofa. She posted the image on her blog, from where it spread to online forum Reddit and became a meme that bounced from college bedrooms to office email chains.

This inspired Dogecoin, which was started as a joke by two software engineers, Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer, and is now the 12th largest cryptocurrency, with a market capitalization of $11.17 billion, according to CoinMarketCap data.

Kabosu, the dog behind the "doge" meme, died in May 2024 after 14 years of internet fame.

#5152. BVNK Opens OUSD Minting and Payments Across Four Blockchains

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: BVNK says eligible business customers can now mint, redeem, hold and transfer Open USD (OUSD) on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo. The November 6 rollout is a practical payments integration, but the company has not provided transaction volumes proving how extensively the new service is being used.

A stablecoin’s biggest hurdle may not be issuing tokens but making them useful inside ordinary financial operations. Payments infrastructure company BVNK has taken a step in that direction by making Open USD accessible through its existing platform.

In a November 6 announcement, BVNK said eligible businesses can mint and redeem OUSD against dollar balances, hold it and transfer it on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo. The product is aimed at payment providers, treasury teams and companies that need to move between bank money and blockchain settlement without assembling separate integrations for every network.

BVNK outlines three routes. A direct integration allows a company to use OUSD in its own treasury and operations. An embedded option lets developers offer wallets, pay-ins or payouts within customer-facing applications. Wholesale access is aimed at exchanges, trading desks and market makers that need larger-scale minting and redemption.

These categories are more important than a promotional claim of being multichain. A business needs clarity about the currency held, when redemption is available, which network is supported and whether the underlying legal and compliance arrangements suit the countries involved. A token arriving quickly on a blockchain is only one step in an end-to-end payment.

BVNK says the launch offers 1:1 conversion against dollar balances and positions OUSD as part of an open-infrastructure model. The firm identifies a consortium of financial and technology companies behind the wider initiative, but membership of a consortium should not be mistaken for a guarantee of liquidity, issuer credit quality or operational support from every named institution.

A company with customers on different chains can otherwise face bridge complexity, additional custody arrangements and fragmented liquidity. Supporting several networks in one interface potentially reduces that operational burden, especially for businesses already using BVNK’s services.

However, crosschain availability does not mean every route is interchangeable or that every address and wallet supports every version of the token. Businesses still have to prevent wrong-network transfers and reconcile balances across chains. The value of the integration will be visible in reliability and error handling, not just a list of supported networks.

For context, NewsBTC has covered how Solana’s settlement tools are being built for institutions. OUSD addresses a related but separate problem: supplying a payment asset and an operating layer through which companies can use it.

BVNK says OUSD is available to eligible business customers outside the European Economic Area. That geographic qualification matters because stablecoin access and licensing rules differ between jurisdictions. Users should check eligibility before assuming they can open a new account or send tokens through a particular network.

The company has not published figures establishing how much OUSD has been minted or transferred specifically through this new integration. For now, the news is a live product capability, not a demonstrated leap in adoption. The next useful evidence would be sustained payment volume, repeat business usage and disclosures about redemption performance during busy markets.

RealFi is targeting a December 1 Ethereum mainnet launch while exploring a possible XRP Ledger expansion.

RealFi plans to launch on Ethereum mainnet on December 1, according to a Cardano-focused host reviewing the project’s expansion plans. The Angry Crypto Show puts the move at the center of a broader question: whether Cardano-originated financial products can attract users and liquidity beyond their home network.

The host cites Token Terminal data showing RealFi has surpassed $121.7 million in asset transfer volume on Cardano. That figure measures transfers, not deposits or total value locked. The transcript does not specify the year of the planned Ethereum launch.

In remarks quoted from an interview with David Gokhshtein, RealFi CEO John O’Connor argues that stablecoins keep growing because they serve a practical purpose: moving stable-value money across borders. He identifies yield-bearing products as the fastest-growing part of that business.

An XRP Ledger expansion is less definite. O’Connor points to the network’s high fully diluted valuation and relatively limited DeFi activity as reasons to explore an integration.

“That’s a conversation we’re kicking off to see whether there’s value for us to come over there,” he says, according to the transcript. No launch date, partnership agreement or technical implementation is announced.

The host sees a potential exchange: Cardano-originated products could gain access to XRP users and liquidity, while offering additional financial functionality. That is the commentator’s investment thesis, not evidence of committed demand.

The video also reports that more than $450,000 worth of bitcoin had been supplied to Cardano’s Strike Finance within eight days of its integration of a bitcoin collateral asset. The figure offers another adoption signal, though the transcript provides no longer-term comparison.

Whether RealFi delivers its announced Ethereum launch, secures integrations and attracts sustained usage. An XRP Ledger expansion could broaden distribution, but O’Connor’s qualification matters – the project wants wider access only where the numbers justify it.

#5150. Robinhood Chain was built for tokenized stocks – But memecoins took over

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Gen Zs are rewriting the rules of wealth creation, increasingly trading the traditional financial playbook for a high-stakes game of chance.

From cryptocurrencies and memecoins to sports betting and prediction markets, the generation is exploring unconventional ways in pursuit of financial gains that once seemed possible only through years of saving and investing.

In this complex financial landscape, the line separating investing from gambling is blurring by the day. In fact, Ashley Embers recently highlighted how 37% of Gen Z respondents engage in sports betting, while 20% place bets online.

More concerningly, over half of Gen Z adults aged 18–29 reportedly redirected money originally intended for investments into sports betting over the past year, with 14% doing so several times a month.

This shift is also being reflected in a few corners of the crypto market, which is even better than memecoins.

One interesting example of this shift is Robinhood Chain.

When Robinhood introduced its Ethereum [ETH] Layer-2 network, the company planned to build a three-in-one infrastructure layer, which includes tokenized stocks, real-world assets [RWAs], and decentralized finance [DeFi] applications.

Expanding on this, Johann Kerbrat, SVP and General Manager of Crypto and International at Robinhood, said,

We’re bringing the best of traditional finance and DeFi together, and in doing so, expanding financial ownership to every corner of the globe.

The main goal of the team was to bring traditional financial markets on-chain to enable users to access tokenized versions of familiar assets through blockchain infrastructure.

However, the network’s early adoption took a complete U-turn from the initial goal. Rather than being primarily driven by tokenized equities and traditional financial products, Robinhood Chain attracted considerable attention from memecoin traders.

Expressing his opinion on the matter, Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev said,

If you hold a memecoin, you just get stock tokens airdropped to you.

This has raised an interesting question: Is Robinhood building the next generation of tokenized financial markets, or has it accidentally created another destination for speculative crypto trading?

Tokenized equities were expected to be one of the Robinhood’s defining use cases. However, the initial trading activity suggested that traders have found another reason to use the network.

Per Bitquery’s analysis of Robinhood Chain’s trading activity between the 16th and the 28th of July 2026, memecoins accounted for approximately 93.5% of trading across 63.5 million transactions. Tokenized equities, meanwhile, represented just 6.5%.

CoinGecko also highlighted this shift in trend. As per its July 2026 assessment, memecoins accounted for 79.2% of Robinhood Chain’s DEX volume, whereas RWAs made up just 9.69%.

These reveal a considerable gap between Robinhood’s intended use case and actual market demand.

Robinhood Chain has also enabled creators to pair their memecoins with tokenized versions of established companies.

This means that tokenized equities are not necessarily being used for traditional investment purposes. Instead, they have become the trading currency through which users speculate on unrelated digital assets.

Similarly, Bloomberg reported that daily trading volume in pairs combining Robinhood stock tokens with memecoins had reached approximately $443 million in early September.

Yet, despite the speculative nature of its activity, Robinhood Chain has recorded impressive growth since its launch. CoinGecko’s Q3 2026 Crypto Industry Report highlighted the network as the third-most-active blockchain within just three months of its public launch.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood Chain generated more than $88.9 billion in trading volume, averaging approximately 9.5 million transactions per day.

Daily trading volume on its native decentralized exchanges also increased from approximately $1.3 million on launch day to a peak of $3.5 billion on the 4th of September.

The company also added approximately $25 million worth of Bitcoin to its corporate balance sheet in October, describing the purchase as an asset-diversification strategy.

These developments indicate that Robinhood’s broader ambitions extend well beyond memecoins.

However, memecoin trading on the Robinhood Chain is not without its risks.

Bitquery’s investigation found that approximately 84% of the nearly 15,000 tokens launched daily never traded again after their initial transaction. The investigation also revealed that three out of every four open trading positions were underwater.

Meanwhile, Fortune subsequently reported that trading volume in these memecoin-stock pairs had fallen by approximately 96% from its early-September peak.

This highlights how quickly speculative enthusiasm disappears. Yet, despite these concerns, it would be premature to conclude that memecoin activity is sabotaging Robinhood’s broader ambitions.

In fact, the silver lining here might be that speculation could be serving as an unexpected entry point into tokenized finance.

Though the company may have succeeded in getting traders through the door, whether they stay for tokenized stocks and RWAs, rather than the next viral memecoin, remains the bigger question on the table.

#5149. Vitalik Buterin Declares Ethereum (ETH) a Store of Value, Not Fee-Burning Token

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum's intrinsic economics is rebuilding itself in motion with tech bugs and the macroeconomic picture overlaying each other in the span of 48 hours. The week wraps up for a major alternative crypto project with a sudden Glamsterdam hard fork stop after testnet launch revealed a dangerous bug in the fee recalculating mechanism, brutally breaking the logic in smart contracts.

As the Ethereum community debated the ability of the network to sustain on old power, Vitalik Buterin showed up with a manifesto which completely zeroes out all the panic around mainnet's decreasing revenue. The "red line" behind Vitalik's updated vision is that the community should stop being fixated on the idea of ETH as "fee-burninng token". For a basic blockchain layer worth $270 billion, attempts to build evaluation on the amount of gas burned are a dead end. For Vitalik, the novel of "ETH as store of value (SoV)" is much more viable amid all the global uncertainty around.

This U-turn, taken by a key visionary of the ecosystem, happened at $2,240 for ETH and may drastically change all the plans developed with a focus on Glamsterdam architecture. The hard fork was initially projected for the logic of blockspace surplus, not the deficit. Ecosystem builders are already readying expansion of L1 capacity with the help of EIP-8037 (tariffs calibration) and EIP-7928 (parallel production) with an aim to raise gas limits up to 200 million units. The logic is that the excess of free space will cheapen the transactions, while token burning rates will gradually be cut.

The market saw a risk of deflation in this concept. Vitalik took a front-step. By his estimates, the historical peaks of burning through EIP-1559 "never were as strong as they seemed". They were dependent on inner cyclical activity of crypto speculations. And it itself was falling once every bear market started.

EIP-1559 is not going anywhere, and Vitalik openly says "don't be sad" if the volume of gas burned will forever stay below the 10% mark. The source of value for Ethereum lies in completely another dimension.

Solana's co-founder, Anatoly Yakovenko, unexpectedly aligned with Buterin on this matter. "You can't focus on fees as the products", he said, calling such an idea "absolutely meaningless". According to Yakovenko, the blockchain network must generate real value for the end users, not control the price of getting into the block.

Vitalik is absolutely right that you can’t focus on fees as the product. That’s absolutely meaningless. You need to pick a product, the thing that brings value to people, and do that really well.

There is lots of technical stuff and philosophy around, but what the missed deadline on the testnet and Vitalik's manifesto reveal is that Ethereum opts for long-term, secure, and even a bit boring stability of the basic layer. Infra doesn't try to flirt with the market through deflationary records.

#5148. The 6 Best Undereye Patches, Tested and Reviewed by Dermatologists and Beauty Editors

The entire Women's Health team swears by them.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’m always up late doomscrolling TikTok and The White Lotus subreddit for season 4 theories. (Natasha Rothwell hive, stand up!) The only problem? Those late nights mean I have dark circles and puffiness in the morning (boo!). While I'm a huge fan of undereye creams, sometimes I get bored and need to switch things up. Enter undereye patches. They're a fast fix for dryness, puffiness, and dark circles—and even help me fake eight hours of sleep. "The skin under the eyes is prone to changes related to aging skin, such as fine lines, and conditions like dryness and discoloration," says dermatologist Brendan Camp, MD. In just 10 to 20 minutes, undereye patches temporarily hydrate the delicate skin and help me look refreshed. Plus, they're super cute and add a fun touch to my selfies, even if they're shared to just my Close Friends circle on Instagram Stories.

Like any other skin care product, eye masks really get their power from their ingredients, some of which are typically hyaluronic acid, vitamin C, niacinamide, and caffeine.

“Eye patches incorporate key ingredients like hyaluronic acid to boost moisture, peptides to firm, ceramides to strengthen the skin barrier, caffeine to help reduce puffiness, and niacinamide to reduce discoloration,” says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD.

As with any beauty product, there are always a few things to consider before making the investment. Since these masks are mostly advertised for their ability to soothe and hydrate, you'll want to check the hydrating and firming ingredients, and keep your expectations realistic since results are usually temporary. Here's what to look out for.

For starters, look for key ingredients such as aloe, chamomile, cucumber, green tea, glycerin, or hyaluronic acid. You're less likely to come across vitamin C and retinol, but it's a plus if you do. Patches with a cellulose gel material can also prevent them from sliding off your face (a con I often deal with and try to avoid as much as possible).

Not only is the skin under your eyes thinner and more delicate than in other areas of your face, but it’s also where lymphatic fluid drainage occurs, says dermatologist Lauren Penzi, MD. It can also show more blood vessels, and in turn, make dark circles appear more visible, says Dr. Garshick. Most eye masks are created to reduce fine lines, undereye darkness, and wrinkles while giving your skin the boost of moisture it needs. The overall effect of these patches is to revive and hydrate, which is why so many people use them to get a more refreshed look.

Many people complain about looking tired, and eye patches are a nice, quick fix. Still, it's important to be realistic about the kind of results you'll get in just one or two uses. So, you’ll want to zero in on the reason you’re buying patches, says Dr. Camp. For example, you can target puffiness by rocking undereye patches infused with caffeine or green tea while getting ready for work, says Dr. Camp.

As a member of the beauty team at Women’s Health, I’m constantly on the hunt for the best products and spend a lot of my time testing and reviewing the latest drops. I frequently consult skin experts, which is exactly what I did to kick off my selection process here. I consulted five New York-based dermatologists and had them give their recommendations with insight on why these undereye masks are so splurge-worthy. Then, I tested several of their picks and compared them to some of the other undereye masks available in our beauty closet.To narrow down the list even further, I got a few other members of team WH, including Addison Aloian, Lily Wohlner, Brian Underwood, and Danielle Jackson, to get in on the testing process. Ingredients, price, and overall efficacy were taken into account to determine which would be best for a wide range of needs and preferences.Here are the fruits of our labor.

After testing tons of undereye masks, this one takes the cake for best overall. Why? It's the most hydrating option on this list and it doesn't slip off your face, which is super hard to find in an undereye mask.

ICYMI, Wander Beauty basically started the undereye mask trend. This OG mask is made with peptides, amino acids, and hyaluronic acid to improve your skin's texture, tone, and hydration. It's also expert-approved by Dr. Garshick and dermatologist Dendy Engelman, MD. "I love that this mask is made with three different layers that allow the formula to penetrate the skin deeply and prevent it from sliding off the face, so you can multitask while you wear it," says Dr. Engelman.

Wander Beauty patches are as effective as they are Instagrammable. I’ve been a fan of the rose gold and yellow gold patches for five years, and all of my beauty editor friends gush over them. They brighten, hydrate, and plump up my fine lines. They also contain calendula extract and aloe vera to help reduce puffiness. Ahem, hi holiday parties and upcoming travel—I’m looking at you.

These pretty patches have three unique layers: the surface's foil retains heat and prevents evaporation, the middle grips to prevent slippage, and the base delivers moisturizing glycerin and depuffing calendula extract. For an extra soothing experience, I like to leave mine in the fridge. Cool temperatures help shrink blood vessels under the eyes, so dark circles appear lighter and puffiness minimizes, dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD, said in our guide to undereye skin care.

That said, the construction of this mask consists of super light and flexible material versus the conventional plastic material found in a lot of other eye patches that were tested, giving this product a high-quality feel.

I would be remiss if I didn't mention my personal fave patch from Patchology. It contains hyaluronic acid (hi, hydrated, plump skin) and feels super cool under the eyes to de-puff and smooth out that area.

Patchology is fantastic for targeting lines, says dermatologist Anar Mikailov, MD. He mentions that there's resveratrol, a natural antioxidant found in grapes that helps improve barrier function, and other antioxidants that provide protection against oxidizing agents that can visibly age the skin by causing wrinkles. There’s also antioxidant-rich strawberry extract, which helps brighten dark circles.

#5147. SWIFT Debuts Own XRP-Inclusive Ledger With Dozen Banks

Home » Ripple (XRP) » SWIFT Debuts Own XRP-Inclusive Ledger With Dozen Banks

Ripple’s XRP extends connections to multiple banks in SWIFT’s blockchain-adopting line-up.

The biggest European financial conglomerate’s grandiose move to release their own blockchain ledger didn’t go unnoticed. This November as planned, the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) debuted the pilot version with 12 banks, some of which are familiar names in the XRP holder community.

One of them, HSBC, is slated to start blockchain-powered operations. HSBC connects its own Tokenised Deposit Service (TDS) to SWIFT’s ledger. The major British bank actively employs Metaco’s Harmonize platform for institutional digital-asset custody (Metaco was acquired by Ripple in 2023). The enterprise-level acquisition strengthened that bond.

5 OF SWIFT'S 17 LEDGER BANKS ALREADY WORK WITH RIPPLE 🚨Swift's new blockchain ledger is live with 17 banks piloting 24/7 cross-border payments.Look who's on that list:🏦 HSBC🏦 Standard Chartered🏦 DBS🏦 FirstRand🏦 BNY, which holds RLUSD's reserves and now holds XRP… https://t.co/z7UOp1KBYz pic.twitter.com/nNP5Ql4vgn

The bank also has historical references to XRPL capabilities in internal materials and some past explorations, with an agenda to expand blockchain-powered business operations. Conducting business operations on Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) based chains like Ripple’s XRP Ledger serves an advantage of instant settlement & cost-effectiveness.

Aside from them, there’s a few more in the 12-long list. Standard Chartered, another popular British bank, has been running the XRP-related tech stack since 2016. During October 2026 the traditional finance behemoth launched their institutional custody for Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger through their Dubai (DIFC) branch.

Also, there’s DBS and BNY (BNY Mellon). These two Ripple-tied major banks serve completely different purposes. BNY Mellon is the primary reserve custodian for RLUSD. Meanwhile, DBS is partnered with Franklin Templeton to list a tokenized money-market fund (sgBENJI) on XRP Ledger, tradeable against RLUSD on their digital exchange.

This is a distinct product from the SWIFT project. SWIFT’s blockchain ledger is compatible with multiple DLT networks, but Ripple’s XRP Ledger has a crystal-clear advantage in regulatory compliance and native traits. XRP, along with Stellar’s XLM & Hedera’s HBAR has native ISO 20022 support, the new gold standard in financial messaging.

The cross-border payments market, worth over $155 trillion in processed volume annually, powers global trade, remittances & commerce. Yet merchants admit it remains slow, costly and not too efficient when compared to blockchain-based counterparts. 70% of merchants expect all transactions to settle immediately by 2027, which aligns with SWIFT’s vision.

However, Ripple’s business ventures don’t always translate into blockchain adoption, as seen in the 2025 example. Ripple Prime, the custody arm, processed over $13 trillion without the help of crypto.

#5146. Flare CEO Pushes Back Against XRP 'FUD'

Flare CEO Hugo Philion has expressed his frustration about recent fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD) around XRP and reiterated that the future of the cryptocurrency should not be centered solely around Ripple.

The Flare CEO recently addressed in an X post the constant habit of XRP holders to evaluate the future of the cryptocurrency through the prism of what Ripple is doing and what it isn't.

"The value and narrative of XRP should never have been viewed as being dependent on the actions of a single actor," the Flare CEO said.

The Flare CEO emphasized that XRP holders should instead concentrate their efforts on finding ways to improve the usability of the cryptocurrency.

In this context, Philion said that XRP holders need to consider three main questions.

The first question is what XRP holders are actually doing to utilize their XRP holdings. The second is how they can convince potential investors to hold XRP.

Finally, the third point that the Flare CEO mentioned is that the XRP community should find a way to transform XRP from a predominantly speculative asset into usable capital.

"And that's part of the reason we created Flare because we feel like there's always been more that can and should be done with XRP," the Flare CEO added.

Besides, the Flare CEO also invited XRP holders to try Flare. According to Philion, it's a way to make XRP less dependent on Ripple.

The Flare CEO's statements come amid increasing frustration around XRP and the lackluster performance of the cryptocurrency.

Over the past year, the price of XRP has gone down by around 50%, and at press time, the price of the cryptocurrency stands at $1.16.

Recently, Ripple's former chief technology officer David Schwartz also faced some criticism over the poor performance of XRP. Schwartz noted that his influence on the XRP price was very limited.

One X user raised a question about whether FLR holders are doing enough to demonstrate the value of the cryptocurrency, especially when it's possible for XRP holders to use Flare's decentralized finance ecosystem without purchasing FLR.

Still, Philion dismissed the claim that there is no need for FLR when using FXRP (a tokenized version of XRP on Flare).

"It's incorrect btw that you can use FXRP without needing FLR," the Flare CEO clarified.

According to Philion, what Flare Smart Accounts do is simply abstract away the need to manage FLR and make the experience more convenient. At the same time, FLR is used to pay transaction fees on the underlying networks.

Besides, the Flare CEO also underlined that in the long term, there should be more use cases for the token apart from transaction fees.

"Usage is important. Need to get fee generation going in a broader way in the ecosystem," he added.

#5144. ChatGPT Is Getting a GIF Maker Powered by OpenAI's Unannounced Images 2.6 Model

ChatGPT Is Getting a GIF Maker Powered by OpenAI's Unannounced Images 2.6 Model

The internet may soon have an unlimited supply of AI-generated dancing cats, courtesy of ChatGPT.

OpenAI is rolling out a feature that lets users generate animated GIFs directly inside ChatGPT, according to The Verge. The feature reportedly comes powered by its new image-generation model called Images 2.6, which OpenAI has yet to formally introduce through its usual product announcements.

Users can describe an animation in plain English or upload an existing photo and ask ChatGPT to bring it to life. Once the GIF is generated, they can adjust its playback speed, inspect individual frames, make edits, and share the finished animation.

OpenAI demonstrated the capability with a simple request: “can you make a gif of a cat dancing?” The resulting interface reportedly includes controls to change animation speed and examine the GIF frame by frame.

We tried generating GIFs using ChatGPT, but the feature was not available on our accounts at the time of testing. In our interaction, the model generates a series of frames, but not the animation.

The rollout appears to be gradual, so users may have to keep asking for their dancing cats a little longer.

The GIF maker is reportedly part of a broader Images 2.6 update that promises faster image generation. The Verge reports that OpenAI is bringing the model to ChatGPT and Codex users across web, desktop, and mobile platforms.

Developers are also getting two new API models, GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst, designed for faster generation and higher-quality results, respectively. OpenAI has not yet published a standalone announcement detailing the new model's capabilities, and we could not independently test its performance.

The update follows the September release of ChatGPT Images 2.5, which introduced sharper details, more precise editing, and generation speeds up to 50% faster than its predecessor.

In our previous testing, Images 2.5 went head-to-head with Google's Nano Banana 2 across six categories, with each model winning three. OpenAI's model delivered particularly impressive illustration quality and improved on the oversharpening problems that affected earlier versions, although it still made mistakes when rendering text.

The move into GIF generation also comes months after OpenAI shut down Sora, its standalone AI video-generation app, in March. Animated GIFs are considerably simpler than the videos Sora generated, but the new feature brings a form of motion generation directly into ChatGPT without requiring a separate application.

OpenAI has not provided a specific date for when every ChatGPT account will receive GIF generation.
